name: Hippocampal Pattern Separation and Completion
short_description: Dentate gyrus performs pattern separation (making similar inputs distinct); CA3 performs pattern completion (reactivating full patterns from partial cues); balance determines discrimination vs generalization
higher_order_principle: The dentate gyrus (DG) performs pattern separation — making similar inputs more distinct to prevent interference. CA3 performs pattern completion — reactivating full stored patterns from partial cues. These two operations are in dynamic tension: too much separation → memories are isolated and don't generalize; too much completion → similar memories interfere and blur together. The balance between separation and completion determines whether similar learning episodes are discriminated or confused.

dentate_gyrus.mechanism: sparse coding — few neurons active for any given input
dentate_gyrus.effect: even slightly different inputs activate non-overlapping DG populations

CA3.mechanism: recurrent connections allow partial cue to reactivate complete stored pattern
CA3.effect: basis of memory retrieval from partial cues

parameters.mechanism: DG sparse coding creates distinct CA3 patterns for similar experiences
parameters.educational_implication: INTERLEAVING works because DG creates distinct codes for each category exemplar when they appear in varied contexts. BLOCKING fails because DG codes are similar within a block → interference.

parameters.mechanism: CA3 recurrent connections (autoassociative network) allow partial cue to reactivate complete stored pattern
parameters.educational_implication: Retrieval practice EXERCISES the pattern completion pathway. Each successful retrieval strengthens the cue → pattern association.

parameters.separation_dominant: high discrimination (can distinguish similar items), low generalization
parameters.completion_dominant: high generalization (sees patterns across cases), low discrimination (confuses similar items)
parameters.educational_note: Novices need separation (distinguish concept A from B). Experts need completion (see pattern across examples). Interleaving promotes separation; blocked practice promotes completion.

scope_conditions: Pattern separation is most critical when learning similar, confusable material
Pattern completion supports retrieval and generalization
Age affects balance: older adults show reduced pattern separation (increased false recognition of similar items)
Stress shifts balance toward pattern completion (reduced discrimination under stress)
moderators: material_similarity (high similarity → greater need for pattern separation)
learning_schedule (interleaving promotes separation; blocking promotes completion)
expertise_level (novices need separation; experts benefit from completion)
age (older adults show reduced pattern separation)

interactions.nature: ED2 operates on the traces created by ED1's binding process.
Retrieval via pattern completion (ED2) triggers reconsolidation (ED3).

ecological_testability: MEDIUM — discrimination/generalization measurable by behavioral tasks (mnemonic similarity task); neural separation/completion measurable by fMRI pattern analysis (representational similarity).
